notes: Pack-wide verification is pending: currency, phone, postcode and IANA zone list were checked against their primary sources; the 32 entity ISO code mapping still needs confirmation in the ISO browser. Names use English and Spanish with engine fallback for other languages; Spanish dictionaries retain their own review status.

The phone example is an intentionally non-dialable placeholder; the RFC example is synthetic and does not assert registration. A format match never verifies a taxpayer, legal representative or licence.

CURP is treated as a sensitive personal identifier by project policy: never display it, index it, export it or send it to counterparties, agents or other hubs. No CURP kind, pattern, example, value or lookup adapter is published. A future private workflow needs a separate reviewed contract and legal basis.
The primary RFC pattern is for legal entities. Sole proprietors use the distinct 13-character tax identifier; personal tax identifiers require privacy review before collection or publication.

The annual holiday list is not a complete election calendar: Labour Law article 74 also covers ordinary election days and the six-year presidential transfer on 1 October. No annual recurrence is invented for those conditional dates. No generic weekend substitution or national working-week schedule is asserted.

Time zones are listed nationally; state-to-zone mappings and border daylight-saving exceptions require location-specific review. Mexico City construction facts apply only to MX-CMX, not all states. Other local construction rules remain unrecorded.

Facets are reference data, not configured services or legal advice. Every adapter is a candidate; no live call, personal lookup, account, payment or provider activation is made. Legal templates are generic and need Mexican counsel review.

MX-CMX is the federal entity Ciudad de Mexico. The v2 schema has no federal-entity kind; district is the available non-state grouping, not a claim that the former Federal District designation remains current.
